newsitem.title: JAPAN: Troubled Japan credit assn gets help from industry.
newsitem.headline: Troubled Japan credit assn gets help from industry.

text.p: Tokyo-based Oji Shinkin Bank said on Thursday that it would merge with financially troubled Musashino Shinkin Bank by the end of March with the support of other credit associations.
"We decided to accept an offer from the Tokyo Association of Shinkin Banks and Zenshinren Bank today," Oji president Koji Ohmae said in a statement.
The merger was done to protect depositors and also aimed at maintaining the credibility of the "shinkin" banking sector, he said.

Shinkin banks are small credit associations which take deposits and lend mainly to members and are supervised by the Ministry of Finance (MOF). They are larger than credit unions, which perform similar tasks, but are supervised by regional governments.

Zenshinren Bank, a national association of credit associations, and Tokyo-based shinkin banks have been working out a plan to bail out Musashino, which is reeling under problem loans estimated at about 39 billion yen. By merging Musashino with a healthy shinkin bank, the sector is keen to prevent the failure from causing further unrest, analysts said.

"The Shinkin banking sector is strongly resolved to help each other solve their bad loan problems in order to make it clear they are different from credit unions," said Yushiro Ikuyo, first vice-president of Smith Barney International Inc.
Credit unions face much bigger troubles with problem loans, he said.

Last summer, Japan's financial system was rocked by a series of financial failures, including the nation's biggest credit union, Kizu Shinyo Kumiai, and the biggest credit union in Tokyo, Cosmo Shinyo Kumiai, due to overlending during the "bubble" era of the late 1980s.
Musashino Shinkin was also saddled with property-related problem loans after the bursting of the bubble economy in the early 1990s.
Yasutaka Miyamoto, chairman of Zenshinren Bank, said at a news conference that no other shinkin bank needed financial support now.

"The shinkin bank sector is relatively healthy compared with other financial sectors. Even if some other shinkin banks fall into trouble, we will be able to cope with the sector's mutual support system."
Musashino Shinkin said at the same news conference that Zenshinren had provided loans to Musashino to help it cope with the outflow of deposits.

Under the bailout plan, Musashino's unrecoverable loans, totalling 28 to 29 billion yen, would be written off by Musashino's capital of five billion yen and aid from the shinkin banks. Musashino's business, including healthy loans and deposits, would be taken over by some shinkins, including Oji.
